summary: Build structured teacher coaching systems and measurable PD programmes. 5-day hands-on course for instructional coaches and school leaders. Enrol now.
lede: Teacher coaching systems connect ongoing classroom support with needs analysis, observation, feedback, and professional learning. Designed for instructional coaches and education leaders, this course develops skills to assess teacher needs and structure coaching cycles, use classroom evidence and student data to guide feedback and goals, and evaluate coaching impact.
audienceIntro: This course is built for education professionals who are already working in or alongside coaching and professional development roles and need a structured system to make that work more consistent, evidence-based, and scalable.
audience: Learning and Development Specialists in education organisations
modules: Teacher Coaching Systems: Foundations and Evidence Base
Teacher Needs Analysis and Competency Mapping
Coaching Conversation Skills and Reflective Practice
Professional Learning Communities: Design and Facilitation
Measuring Coaching Impact and Reporting to Leadership
Building a School-Wide PD System: Strategy and Action Planning
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course. Participants are expected to have at least two years of experience in a teaching, coaching, mentoring, or instructional leadership role. You should be familiar with basic classroom observation practices and have some exposure to professional development planning, even if informal. No advanced data analysis or technology skills are required — digital tools are introduced at an operational level, and all datasets used in exercises are provided. Participants are encouraged to bring a copy of their current school's PD plan or coaching framework (if one exists) to use as a reference point during the needs analysis and capstone exercises.
